result: The proof attempt reduced the conjecture to an explicit constant sandwich and the sandwich DOES NOT CLOSE from the available inputs: the cliff gives core <= 12C; locality gives C <= n K^2 c(a) with c(a) = a^2(1+a^2)/(1-a^2)^3; irreducibility-with-connectivity needs core ~ n AND forces K a >= 1/sqrt(2) (a unitary connecting indices at distance 1 has a 1/sqrt(2) entry), i.e., K >= 1/(sqrt(2)a). Combined: 12 K^2 c(a) >= 6.25 at every a tested (a = 0.1-0.3) — the bound NEVER drops below 1, so the cliff cannot exclude irreducibility at the constant level. The conjecture is GENUINELY OPEN, not a missed pigeonhole: the two n-linear bounds are compatible. Closing requires a finer argument (extracting sub-linear S control from the truncation-BUDGET structure rather than entry locality — the budget a^L decays in L, which entry-locality ignores) or a boundary counterexample (an irreducible family whose typed budgets stay geometric — for which the near-MASA + connectivity tension is exactly the construction site).

The optimized L-balance improves on the trivial n^3 bound by ~2-3 orders (5e4-1e5 vs 1.7e7 at k up to 1000) but remains n-dependent and k-growing. BOTH routes (entry-locality; budget structure) leave the no-irreducible-member conjecture genuinely open. Noisy control characterized: the hidden-symmetry direction survives noise as a sub-bulk singular value (0.0077/0.0397/0.0768 at eps=0.01/0.05/0.10 vs bulk floor ~0.27-0.29) — a 2-3.5x separation at the tested noise levels. Honest limit: at larger noise the signal merges into the bulk; the instrument detects hidden symmetry robustly to ~10% entry noise at this size. Remaining: the unknown-control, the emitter + timing (the kill test).

Honest correction: the bulk-floor threshold as-parameterized OVER-DETECTS (dim 13-20 across eps 0-0.15 vs the true 2) — the median-based bulk estimate is pulled down by the spread of small-but-non-signal singulars, so the 0.5x threshold swallows them. The underlying noise characterization STANDS (the signal direction is sub-bulk by 2-3.5x at eps <= 0.1, measured on the actual singular values), but the automatic dimension call needs a proper bulk estimator (upper-quantile or two-cluster fit on the log-spectrum). Logged per discipline; the fix is the next instrument iteration.

Two fixes tested: quantile-bulk (over-detects ~300, worse — disclosed) and two-cluster log-spectrum k-means: EXACT at eps=0 (dim 2, three seeds) and on the negative control (dim 1); at eps>0 it returns 1 (the scalar) — CONSERVATIVE under noise: it never over-detects, and the hidden direction (measured sub-bulk by 2-3.5x) sits between the clusters and is not claimed. Honest characterization: the instrument is now SOUND (no false positives at any tested noise; exact in the clean case) with noise-limited RECALL — it certifies detected symmetry when found but declines to claim it under moderate noise. This is the right failure mode for an instrument feeding arithmetic (a false positive would corrupt the arithmetic; a miss just forfeits the speedup). Remaining: the unknown-control, the emitter + timing.

The instruments H1 evidence: detected structure converts to measured arithmetic advantage. Kill rule NOT triggered.

Full instrument verdict: detection exact on positive/negative/unknown controls (the hidden C3-in-random-basis detected at dim 3); noise behavior sound (conservative); emitter verified with measured 8-12x. Kill rule NOT triggered; the instrument unit closes as a working prototype with the structure-recovery refinement (full centralizer algebra, not single elements) as the named next step.

Timing correction (the 8x claim was WRONG): the adapted arithmetic with einsum transforms measured 272ms vs dense 2.6ms (0.0x — einsum on 4-index tensors is catastrophically slow); with matrix-form transforms: measured honestly below. The 8x earlier measurement compared dense against per-block powers ONLY (excluding transforms) — retracted. Honest verdict: at N=288 with nb=12 blocks, per-block powers are cheap but the transform overhead dominates: NO measured advantage at this size. The advantage regime is LARGE chains (transform cost amortized over many compositions) or repeated products — the timing test must be rerun in that regime before any claim. The instruments detection results all stand; only the timing claim is corrected.

Root cause of the 0.1-0.2x measurements found: the emitter was applying the adapted basis as a DENSE kron matrix (two N^3 GEMMs per member — the FFT structure never used, measured 77.5ms vs the true axis-FFT 20.8ms per transform pair). INSTRUMENT VERDICT: detection works (all controls); the ARITHMETIC ADVANTAGE is unrealized at NumPy level; a C/BLAS-fused implementation could realize the theory margin but is a separate build.
